Performing a manipulation of the argument account/password results in os command injection. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

Dokploy before 0.31.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in getComposeContainerCommand() that allows authenticated organization members to execute shell commands via the serviceName parameter. Attackers can store serviceName values with shell metacharacters through backup.create or backup.update tRPC procedures, executing commands as root when scheduled backups run and taking over the host via the mounted Docker socket.

This issue affects the function exec/system of the file modules/assets/port_serve_scan.mds of the component Web Management UI. This manipulation of the argument task_name/where/path causes os command injection. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
SQL injection in the Core of Ivanti Endpoint Manager before version 2024 SU8 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to achieve remote code execution.

OS command injection in the example SSM document provisioning script in Trusted Remote Execution (REX) before 2026-07-28 might allow an authenticated remote user who is permitted to invoke the Rex-RO or Rex-RW SSM document to execute arbitrary commands as root on the managed instance, bypassing Cedar policy enforcement. To remediate this issue, users should delete any Rex-RO and Rex-RW SSM documents created from the example script, in each account and Region where it was run.

build-git-clone before 1.0.4 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the clone() function that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying crafted repository URLs. Attackers can embed shell metacharacters such as ; or $() in the url argument, which is concatenated into a sh -c command, to execute operating system commands with Node.js process privileges.

Craft CMS 4.0.0 before 4.18.9 and 5.0.0 before 5.11.2 contains an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the element search endpoint because the attribute parameter is concatenated into the query unsanitized and emulated PDO prepares allow stacked statements. Remote attackers can read and write the database, setting the admin flag or overwriting password hashes in the users table to gain administrator access.

The manipulation of the argument remoteIp results in command injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks.

ThinkPHP 5.0.0 before 5.0.24 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute commands by setting _method=__construct in POST data to overwrite the Request filter property. Attackers can send POST requests to endpoints reached via ?s=captcha or ?s=index/index/index with filter[]=system and server[REQUEST_METHOD] values to execute arbitrary system commands. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

SolarWinds Dameware was found to be affected by a command injection vulnerability that could lead to the compromise of the remotely controlled host. Authentication is required.
